request.brief: WW1 focus for Imperial Japan, 1910-1918. Focus ID JP1_R_air_army_air_coordination. Display title: Air Reports for the Gun Line. Context: Observers and artillery staffs will agree on signals, reports and target handover. Aircraft can support the infantry only when the men on the ground understand what the pilots are telling them. Actual completion effects (interpret their meaning, never draw code or words): completion_reward = { add_mastery_bonus = { name = JP1_R_air_army_air_coordination bonus = 0.1 days = 240 track = strike_aircraft } } Prerequisite context: prerequisite = { focus = JP1_R_air_first_recon } Choose one large historically appropriate object or one coherent emblem that directly communicates this focus's specific action and reward. Every focus gets its own composition; avoid a generic symbol whose subject is unrelated. Identity where appropriate: authentic national dress, architecture, period heraldry or a restrained national enamel accent, only of Imperial Japan. No country maps or silhouettes. No communist symbols unless this specific focus explicitly promotes communism. No modern equipment or WW2 motifs. Use contemporary vanilla Paradox national focus rendering: sharp clean sculpted relief, smooth metal and enamel, controlled selective highlights, deep solid shadows, no rusty weathering, noisy grain, mottled patina or rough brush texture. Match the attached vanilla reference's rendering quality, not its subject. A complete opaque dark enamel backing and precise beveled metal frame are required. Vary the shape and colour to fit the subject and nationality: shield, diamond, clipped rectangle or medallion, avoid repeating an identical frame for every focus. Center the subject, let it fill most of the frame, keep a small clean transparent outside margin. No transparent gaps through the backplate. At 100x88, use few large shapes and avoid tiny floating overlays or a heap of unrelated objects. No lettering, numbers, writing, watermarks or signatures.

Requirements:
- Take the frame, outline and overall form from the style anchor images, not from a fixed family form; the size, transparency, margin and readability requirements here still apply.
- Flags and ribbons use invented colours, never a real country's flag, unless the brief names that country.
- The subject is large: it fills most of the emblem and may overlap its frame, never a small figure inside a wide empty plaque.
- A strong central symbol that supports the focus's story, readable contrast at 100x88 pixels.
- Real transparent background around the emblem: no backdrop behind it.
- Leave a small empty margin around the emblem.

Reference images, in the order attached:
1. style anchor: match its painting style, palette and level of detail
The style anchor images were chosen for this image. Match their form, framing, materials and palette; the vanilla form described under Requirements applies only where they do not show one.

Avoid: text; letters or numbers; watermark or signature; a drawn checkerboard pattern; a square backdrop behind the subject.

Produce exactly one image.
